main_body: Snow-covered log cabin: a large snowy roof slope (rows ~7-50) above a wooden plank front wall (rows ~52-77) with an arched double door, two lit windows and round wreaths.
top_band: Pale white/light-blue snow roof slope, rows ~8-50 at the middle column, with a lighter front-edge band at rows ~47-50 (eave); it is the lightest tone and sits above the wall face.
evidence: The roof is a large foreshortened slope drawn as a wide surface with snow courses and a distinct light eave edge at rows 47-50, followed by dark shadow and icicles at rows 51-53 over the vertical plank wall. The door has an arch with iron straps and the windows have snow sills and lintels, which read as inset. It matches the Beodeul house pattern of a roof slope above a wall face, so the structure passes.

style.evidence: The snow roof uses about 5 blue-white steps with per-course shadow scallops, clumps and an icy eave. The wood wall has varied brown planks with dark brown separation, and there are icicles, wreaths and snow drifts at the base. The outlines are dark navy and brown, tinted to the neighbouring material rather than neutral black. There are no large flat fills and the detail density is comparable to the references.
